intro: Hi! You already talk about the past with was and were. Now you'll talk about actions in the past: I walked, she cooked, we stayed, with the small ending -ed, how to spell it and how to say it. You'll also learn yesterday, last week and two days ago. Warm-up: tell me about last night. Try 'I watched TV' or 'I cooked dinner'.
teachingNotes: Indonesian never changes the verb for time: 'Kemarin saya jalan kaki ke kantor' uses the same 'jalan' as today; only kemarin, tadi, minggu lalu (or sudah) show the past. English changes the verb: walk → walked. The #1 error is *'Yesterday I walk to work': whenever the learner uses yesterday, last … or … ago, check the verb has -ed. A second common error comes from the last lesson: *'I was walk / I was cook dinner'. was/were is the past of am/is/are only, not a past marker for other verbs. The past form is the same for every person: I walked, she walked, they walked (no -s: not *'she walkeds' or *'she walks yesterday').

Spelling: most verbs + ed (worked, cleaned); vowel + y also just + ed (played, stayed, enjoyed); ends in -e → + d (lived, danced, liked); consonant + y → ied (studied, tried, carried): stress *'studyed', the node's common error. Doubling: only short one-beat verbs ending in one vowel + one consonant (stop → stopped, plan → planned, shop → shopped, chat → chatted); explain why: 'stoped' would look like it's said 'stoupt', like 'hoped'. Longer verbs stressed at the front just add -ed (visited, opened, listened), and w, x, y are never doubled (fixed, played, snowed). British travelled / cancelled, American traveled / canceled: both correct.

Pronunciation, by the LAST SOUND of the verb (like the -s ending from a1-pron-endings): 't' after sounds with no buzz, p, k, f, s, sh, ch, x (worked 'workt', stopped 'stopt', danced 'danst', liked 'laikt'); 'd' after vowels and buzzing sounds (played 'pleid', lived 'livd', cleaned 'kliind'); 'id', one extra beat, ONLY after t or d (wanted 'WON-tid', needed 'NII-did', visited 'VI-zi-tid'). Commonest errors: an extra beat everywhere ('work-ed', 'play-ed') and dropping the ending so walk and walked sound the same. Never show bare IPA; give the everyday spelling. Deeper -ed and weak-form practice comes in a2-pron-ed-weak-forms.

Time markers: yesterday (morning / afternoon), last night / week / month / year / weekend / Sunday (no 'the', no 'on': *'on last Sunday', *'the last week'), and length of time + ago (two days ago, an hour ago), counting back from now. Indonesian 'lalu' maps to both: no number → last (minggu lalu = last week), with a number → ago (dua minggu lalu = two weeks ago). Stress the node's common error *'two years before': before needs something after it (before lunch). 'tadi malam / kemarin malam' = last night (not 'yesterday night'); 'tadi pagi' = this morning. The time word can go at the start or the end.

Limits: positive sentences with regular verbs only. Don't teach negatives or questions with did/didn't (that's a2-past-simple-irregular); when you ask the learner about their past, use prompts like 'Tell me about yesterday' rather than 'What did you do?' if they struggle. Don't teach irregular past forms (went, had, saw, ate): if the learner uses one correctly, accept it; if they write 'goed' or 'eated', give the right form and say these verbs come in the next lesson. No present perfect (I have visited) and no years (not taught yet): use yesterday, last … and … ago.

keyPoints.title: Past simple: verb + -ed (spelling and sound)
keyPoints.explanation: For a finished action in the past, add -ed to the verb: walk → walked. Same form for everyone (I/she/they walked), and no was before it. Spelling: + ed (worked, played); ends in -e → + d (lived); consonant + y → ied (studied); short verb with one vowel + one consonant → double it (stopped). Sound: 't' after p, k, f, s, sh, ch, x (worked = 'workt'); 'd' after vowels and buzzing sounds (played = 'pleid'); an extra beat 'id' only after t or d (wanted = 'WON-tid').

id.title: Past simple: kata kerja + -ed (ejaan dan bunyi)
id.explanation: Untuk kegiatan yang sudah selesai di masa lalu, tambahkan -ed pada kata kerja: walk → walked. Bentuknya sama untuk semua orang (I/she/they walked), dan tanpa was di depannya. Ejaan: + ed (worked, played); berakhiran -e → + d (lived); konsonan + y → ied (studied); kata kerja pendek dengan satu vokal + satu konsonan → huruf terakhir digandakan (stopped). Bunyi: 't' setelah p, k, f, s, sh, ch, x (worked = 'workt'); 'd' setelah bunyi vokal dan bunyi yang bergetar (played = 'pleid'); tambahan satu ketukan 'id' hanya setelah t atau d (wanted = 'WON-tid').

keyPoints.title: Time words: yesterday, last …, … ago
keyPoints.explanation: yesterday (morning / afternoon); last + night / week / month / year / Sunday, with no 'the' and no 'on'; a length of time + ago: two days ago, an hour ago (ago comes after and counts back from now). Indonesian 'lalu' is both: minggu lalu = last week, dua minggu lalu = two weeks ago. Not 'two years before'.

examples.en: We stayed in Bandung last weekend.
examples.id: Kami menginap di Bandung akhir pekan lalu.

examples.en: Rina called me an hour ago.
I visited Bali two years ago.

id.title: Kata waktu: yesterday, last …, … ago
id.explanation: yesterday (morning / afternoon); last + night / week / month / year / Sunday, tanpa 'the' dan tanpa 'on'; lamanya waktu + ago: two days ago, an hour ago (ago ada di belakang dan dihitung mundur dari sekarang). Kata 'lalu' dalam bahasa Indonesia bisa jadi keduanya: minggu lalu = last week, dua minggu lalu = two weeks ago. Bukan 'two years before'.

blocks.text:
In Indonesian the **verb** (the doing word: *jalan, kerja, masak*) never changes for time. *Saya jalan kaki ke kantor* can be today or yesterday: only a time word like *kemarin*, *tadi* or *minggu lalu* (or *sudah*) tells you it's the past.

English changes the verb itself: add **-ed**. *Kemarin saya jalan kaki ke kantor* → **Yesterday I walked to the office.** This is the **past simple**: an action that happened and finished at a time in the past (yesterday, last week, two days ago).

id.text:
Dalam bahasa Indonesia, **kata kerja** (kata yang menunjukkan kegiatan: *jalan, kerja, masak*) tidak pernah berubah karena waktu. *Saya jalan kaki ke kantor* bisa hari ini atau kemarin: hanya kata waktu seperti *kemarin*, *tadi* atau *minggu lalu* (atau *sudah*) yang menunjukkan itu masa lalu.

Bahasa Inggris mengubah kata kerjanya sendiri: tambahkan **-ed**. *Kemarin saya jalan kaki ke kantor* → **Yesterday I walked to the office.** Ini namanya **past simple**: kegiatan yang terjadi dan sudah selesai pada suatu waktu di masa lalu (yesterday, last week, two days ago).

blocks.text:
Two traps:
- The past form is **the same for everyone**: *I walked, she walked, they walked*. The **-s** of *she works* is only for now, so not 'she workeds'.
- **Don't put was/were before the verb**: 'I was cook dinner' ✗ → **I cooked dinner**. *was/were* is the past of *am/is/are* only (*I was tired*), not a past sign for every verb.

A few common verbs don't take -ed (*go, have, eat*). You'll learn them in the next lesson.

id.text:
Dua jebakan:
- Bentuk lampaunya **sama untuk semua orang**: *I walked, she walked, they walked*. Huruf **-s** di *she works* hanya untuk sekarang, jadi bukan 'she workeds'.
- **Jangan taruh was/were di depan kata kerja**: 'I was cook dinner' ✗ → **I cooked dinner**. *was/were* hanya bentuk lampau dari *am/is/are* (*I was tired*), bukan tanda masa lalu untuk semua kata kerja.

Ada beberapa kata kerja umum yang tidak memakai -ed (*go, have, eat*). Kamu akan mempelajarinya di pelajaran berikutnya.

blocks.prompt: Last Saturday my brother ___ the car.
blocks.explain: Last Saturday is a finished time in the past, so wash + ed: washed. 'was wash' mixes was with another verb, and 'washes' is for now.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Last Saturday my brother ___ the car.
id.explain: Last Saturday itu waktu yang sudah lewat, jadi wash + ed: washed. 'was wash' mencampur was dengan kata kerja lain, dan 'washes' untuk sekarang.

id.title: Kegiatan yang sudah selesai: kata kerja + -ed

blocks.text:
First, two words: **vowels** are the letters *a, e, i, o, u*; **consonants** are all the other letters (*b, c, d, k, l, n, p, r, t …*). Now the four rules:
- **Most verbs: + ed.** *work → worked, clean → cleaned, play → played.*
- **Ends in e: just + d.** *live → lived, dance → danced, like → liked.*
- **Consonant + y: y → ied.** *study → studied, try → tried.* But **vowel + y** just takes -ed: *play → played, stay → stayed, enjoy → enjoyed.*
- **Short verb of one beat, ending in one vowel + one consonant: double the last letter.** *stop → stopped, shop → shopped, chat → chatted, drop → dropped.* Why? Without the double letter, *stoped* would look like *hoped*, which is said 'houpt'. The double letter keeps the short 'o' of *stop*.

id.text:
Pertama, dua istilah: **vokal** adalah huruf *a, e, i, o, u*; **konsonan** adalah semua huruf lainnya (*b, c, d, k, l, n, p, r, t …*). Sekarang empat aturannya:
- **Kebanyakan kata kerja: + ed.** *work → worked, clean → cleaned, play → played.*
- **Berakhiran e: cukup + d.** *live → lived, dance → danced, like → liked.*
- **Konsonan + y: y → ied.** *study → studied, try → tried.* Tapi **vokal + y** cukup + ed: *play → played, stay → stayed, enjoy → enjoyed.*
- **Kata kerja pendek satu ketukan, berakhiran satu vokal + satu konsonan: gandakan huruf terakhirnya.** *stop → stopped, shop → shopped, chat → chatted, drop → dropped.* Kenapa? Tanpa huruf ganda, *stoped* akan terlihat seperti *hoped*, yang dibaca 'houpt'. Huruf ganda menjaga bunyi 'o' pendek dari *stop*.

rows.note: one beat, o + p → double the p

id.note: satu ketukan, o + p → p digandakan

rows.note: no double: VI-sit is strong at the front

id.note: tidak digandakan: VI-sit kuat di depan

blocks.text:
Why *visited* and not 'visitted'? The double-letter rule is for **short verbs of one beat** (*stop, shop, chat*). Longer verbs that are said strong at the front (*VI-sit, O-pen, LIS-ten*) just add -ed: *visited, opened, listened*. And **w, x, y are never doubled**: *fixed, played, snowed*.

British and American spelling differ in a few verbs: **travelled / cancelled** (British), **traveled / canceled** (American). Both are correct.

id.text:
Kenapa *visited*, bukan 'visitted'? Aturan huruf ganda hanya untuk **kata kerja pendek satu ketukan** (*stop, shop, chat*). Kata kerja yang lebih panjang dan diucapkan kuat di depan (*VI-sit, O-pen, LIS-ten*) cukup + ed: *visited, opened, listened*. Dan **w, x, y tidak pernah digandakan**: *fixed, played, snowed*.

Ejaan Inggris (British) dan Amerika berbeda di beberapa kata kerja: **travelled / cancelled** (British), **traveled / canceled** (Amerika). Keduanya benar.

blocks.text:
The -ed ending is written the same way, but it has **three sounds**. It works like the -s ending you know (*works, plays, watches*). Listen to the **last sound** of the verb, not the last letter:
- **'t'** (written /t/): after sounds with **no buzz** in your throat: *p, k, f, s, sh, ch, x*. *worked* is said 'workt', *stopped* 'stopt', *liked* 'laikt', *danced* 'danst' (dance ends in an 's' sound).
- **'d'** (written /d/): after vowel sounds and sounds **with a buzz**: *b, g, l, m, n, r, v, z*. *played* is said 'pleid', *lived* 'livd', *cleaned* 'kliind', *called* 'kold'.
- **'id'** (written /ɪd/): **only after t or d**. This adds one more **beat** (syllable, *suku kata*): *wanted* 'WON-tid', *needed* 'NII-did', *visited* 'VI-zi-tid'.

With 't' and 'd', the verb keeps its beats: *worked* is one beat, like *work*.

id.text:
Akhiran -ed selalu ditulis sama, tapi punya **tiga bunyi**. Cara kerjanya mirip akhiran -s yang sudah kamu kenal (*works, plays, watches*). Dengarkan **bunyi terakhir** kata kerjanya, bukan huruf terakhirnya:
- **'t'** (ditulis /t/): setelah bunyi yang **tidak bergetar** di tenggorokan: *p, k, f, s, sh, ch, x*. *worked* dibaca 'workt', *stopped* 'stopt', *liked* 'laikt', *danced* 'danst' (dance berakhir dengan bunyi 's').
- **'d'** (ditulis /d/): setelah bunyi vokal dan bunyi yang **bergetar**: *b, g, l, m, n, r, v, z*. *played* dibaca 'pleid', *lived* 'livd', *cleaned* 'kliind', *called* 'kold'.
- **'id'** (ditulis /ɪd/): **hanya setelah t atau d**. Ini menambah satu **ketukan** (suku kata): *wanted* 'WON-tid', *needed* 'NII-did', *visited* 'VI-zi-tid'.

Dengan 't' dan 'd', jumlah ketukannya tetap: *worked* satu ketukan, sama seperti *work*.

blocks.text:
Two common mistakes:
- **An extra beat everywhere**: 'work-ed', 'play-ed', 'clean-ed' ✗. Only verbs ending in a t or d sound get 'id'.
- **Dropping the ending**: in Indonesian a t or d at the end of a word is very soft, so *I walk* and *I walked* can sound the same. Say the small 't' or 'd' clearly.

The throat test: put your hand on your throat and say *sss*, then *zzz*. 'zzz' buzzes, 'sss' doesn't. No buzz before -ed → 't'; buzz → 'd'.

id.text:
Dua kesalahan yang sering terjadi:
- **Menambah ketukan di semua kata**: 'work-ed', 'play-ed', 'clean-ed' ✗. Hanya kata kerja yang berakhiran bunyi t atau d yang mendapat 'id'.
- **Akhirannya hilang**: dalam bahasa Indonesia, t atau d di akhir kata diucapkan sangat lembut, jadi *I walk* dan *I walked* bisa terdengar sama. Ucapkan 't' atau 'd' kecil itu dengan jelas.

Tes tenggorokan: taruh tanganmu di tenggorokan, ucapkan *sss*, lalu *zzz*. 'zzz' bergetar, 'sss' tidak. Tidak bergetar sebelum -ed → 't'; bergetar → 'd'.

blocks.explain: need ends in a d sound, so -ed is said 'id' and adds a beat: NII-did, two beats.

id.prompt: Ada berapa ketukan (suku kata) di kata 'needed'?
id.explain: need berakhiran bunyi d, jadi -ed dibaca 'id' dan menambah satu ketukan: NII-did, dua ketukan.

blocks.text:
A time word tells the listener **when**. With the past simple you often use:
- **yesterday** (*kemarin*), **yesterday morning / afternoon** (*kemarin pagi / siang*).
- **last** + night / week / month / year / weekend / Sunday: *last week* (*minggu lalu*). No *the* and no *on*: **last Sunday**, not 'on last Sunday'.
- a length of time + **ago**: *two days ago* (*dua hari yang lalu*), *an hour ago* (*sejam yang lalu*). **ago** counts back from now, and it comes **after** the length of time: not 'ago two days'.

The time word can go at the end or at the start: *I called Budi yesterday.* / *Yesterday I called Budi.*

id.text:
Kata waktu memberi tahu pendengar **kapan**. Dengan past simple kamu sering memakai:
- **yesterday** (*kemarin*), **yesterday morning / afternoon** (*kemarin pagi / siang*).
- **last** + night / week / month / year / weekend / Sunday: *last week* (*minggu lalu*). Tanpa *the* dan tanpa *on*: **last Sunday**, bukan 'on last Sunday'.
- lamanya waktu + **ago**: *two days ago* (*dua hari yang lalu*), *an hour ago* (*sejam yang lalu*). **ago** dihitung mundur dari sekarang, dan letaknya **sesudah** lamanya waktu: bukan 'ago two days'.

Kata waktunya bisa di akhir atau di awal kalimat: *I called Budi yesterday.* / *Yesterday I called Budi.*

blocks.text:
Indonesian **lalu** has two English partners:
- no number → **last**: *minggu lalu* = **last week**, *tahun lalu* = **last year**;
- with a number → **ago**: *dua minggu lalu* = **two weeks ago**.

Don't use **before** for this: 'two years before' ✗ → **two years ago**. *before* needs something after it: *before lunch* (sebelum makan siang), *before work*.

And *tadi malam / kemarin malam* = **last night** (English speakers almost never say 'yesterday night'); *tadi pagi* = **this morning**.

id.text:
Kata **lalu** dalam bahasa Indonesia punya dua pasangan dalam bahasa Inggris:
- tanpa angka → **last**: *minggu lalu* = **last week**, *tahun lalu* = **last year**;
- dengan angka → **ago**: *dua minggu lalu* = **two weeks ago**.

Jangan pakai **before** untuk ini: 'two years before' ✗ → **two years ago**. *before* butuh sesuatu sesudahnya: *before lunch* (sebelum makan siang), *before work* (sebelum kerja).

Lalu *tadi malam / kemarin malam* = **last night** (penutur bahasa Inggris hampir tidak pernah bilang 'yesterday night'); *tadi pagi* = **this morning**.
